short_description: Tiny non-enveloped calicivirus (~38-40 nm) whose T=3 icosahedral capsid is built from 180 copies of the single protein VP1 arranged as 90 arch-shaped dimers over a contiguous shell, giving the family its 32 cup-shaped surface hollows (Latin calix = cup); it packs one continuous ~7.5 kb positive-sense ssRNA with VPg on its 5' end plus a few copies of VP2, infects small-intestinal enterocytes, needs only ~10-100 particles to infect, and — being naked — shrugs off alcohol hand gel while soap and water still remove it.

colour_legend.s_domain: muted slate periwinkle-blue (the contiguous inner shell)
colour_legend.p1_subdomain: desaturated sage-teal (the leg of each arch)
colour_legend.p2_subdomain: dusty rose / muted plum (the outer head of each arch, HBGA-binding)
colour_legend.calix: deep shadowed indigo-grey hollow (the 32 cup-shaped depressions)
colour_legend.vpg: small deep indigo bead at the 5' end of the RNA
colour_legend.vp2: pale ochre-mustard minor protein, a few copies against the inner shell face
colour_legend.background: neutral dark charcoal (watercolour: warm aged cream paper)
colour_legend.note: A virion has no pigment of its own; electron microscopes image in greyscale, so every colour here is teaching convention (see reference/colors.md). The chosen CDC PHIL reference is a digitally colorized negative-stain TEM. Keep this same structure->colour mapping in all four styles (textbook, sem, 3d, watercolor) so the set reads as one poster.

do_not_draw: ANY lipid envelope, membrane bilayer, soap-bubble halo or greasy coat around the capsid - norovirus is NAKED / non-enveloped; this is the single most common and most serious error

coronavirus-style long stalked club spikes, a corona of knobs on stalks, HA/NA-style projections, radiating rays, or a fuzzy fringe - the surface relief is only the arching P-domain dimers of the shell itself, never spikes
a smooth featureless sphere, a plain golf ball, a billiard ball or a bare geometric d20 die with no cups or dimples - the 32 cup-shaped hollows and the 90 arches must read clearly
a helical, rod-shaped, filamentous or pleomorphic capsid - the particle is a round-to-hexagonal icosahedron
DNA, a double helix, base-pair rungs or a ladder-shaped genome - the genome is single-stranded RNA
a segmented genome, several separate RNA pieces, or 11 little rods (that is rotavirus) - norovirus has exactly ONE continuous RNA molecule
a triple-layered rotavirus-style shell (inner core + VP6 middle layer + VP7 outer layer), VP4 spikes, or a wheel/hub-and-spoke silhouette - norovirus has a SINGLE capsid layer
a packaged RNA polymerase, a matrix layer, a helical nucleocapsid, or nucleoprotein beads strung along the RNA
a bacteriophage head-and-tail body, tail fibres, base plate or legs
a nucleus, ribosomes, mitochondria, cytoplasm or any cell organelle - a virion is not a cell
a cell wall, peptidoglycan layer, flagellum, pilus or capsule
a face, eyes, mouth or any anthropomorphism (that belongs only on the separate kids' coloring page)
any baked-in text, letters, numbers, labels, arrows, scale bars, rulers, legends or watermarks
a black border, dark frame, vignette, letterbox bar, mat, drop shadow, or the artwork drawn as a sheet/card lying on a surface

reference.note: Digitally-colorized TEM of a cluster of norovirus virions (purple particles on an orange stain background). It is a cluster rather than one isolated particle, but the individual ~30-40 nm capsids are cleanly separated and their knobbly, dimpled, feathery surface relief is plainly readable, and several particles sit free at the edges - so a single specimen can be cropped out. Perfect for showing 'not a smooth sphere' and 'no envelope, no spikes'. PHIL 10704 is the identical greyscale original.
